chapter: Records, rivals and New Orleans bands
title: Johnny Dunn's lack of swing and George Mitchell
summary: Punch says Dunn only played behind singers and could not swing; Allen admires Mitchell's sound.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What trumpet players had the best syncopation and rhythm and all that in those times?

Well I can say that such fellow Johnny Dunn played a nice horn but he wasn't a swing man. But you know, I mean he just played a lot of stuff. But he wasn't a swing man. He'd come here with Mamie Smith and these boys got playing around here and he said he had to go back and run over again. Because he didn't do nothing but play behind singers, see? Like I was showing you, she'd sing and he'd hit a few notes behind her and stop and she'd sing something and he'd hit a few notes. And he'd hit a clean swing out like that, he wasn't doing that. He couldn't do it. He didn't know how to do it.
I took a liking to this George Mitchell. He used to play with the Red Hot Peppers. Yeah. And I wish I could imitate his sound.
Yeah, he was a nice trumpet man.
Still could be. I think he could do it again if he had a chance. Might come by.
